game.title: Game 1: Urgent or Fake Urgent?
game.subtitle: Distinguish actual urgency from things that just sound loud
game.description: Teach participants to assess true business impact and deadlines rather than panicking over loud requests.

questions.title: The Quadruple Ping
questions.scenario:
It is 10:15 AM. You are preparing your slides for an 11:30 AM school session. Four notifications pop up simultaneously:

🔴 A mentor pings: 'Need urgent confirmation if you can take an extra class at 2:00 PM today.'
🟠 A teammate asks: 'Can you review my Scratch project before my class in 3 hours?'
🟡 Admin reminder: 'Submit your weekly attendance log before 5:00 PM today.'
🔥 WhatsApp group message: 'URGENT!! Need someone to update the slide deck ASAP!!'

Which task do you address FIRST?

options.text: Drop everything and fix the 'URGENT!!' slide deck.
Help your teammate review their Scratch project immediately.
Complete your 11:30 AM preparation first, then reply to the mentor about the 2:00 PM class.
Rush to fill in the weekly attendance log to get admin off your back.

questions.explanation: Your immediate commitment is the 11:30 AM class happening in 75 minutes. The mentor's 2:00 PM request has a clear time window, whereas 'URGENT' without context or deadline is often fake urgency.
questions.learningObjective: Prioritize by real deadline & direct classroom impact, not by who types in ALL CAPS.
questions.discussionQuestion: Why do we instinctively jump to whoever writes 'URGENT' in capital letters?
questions.facilitatorTips: Ask the room: 'Who chose A? Why does the word URGENT trigger panic?'

dynamicUpdate.announcement: 🚨 PLOT REVEAL: The person who sent 'URGENT!! slide deck' actually needs it for next Thursday's marketing meeting!
dynamicUpdate.questionText: Now that you know this, what is the professional rule for incoming 'urgent' tasks?

options.text: Ignore all WhatsApp messages forever.
Always ask: 'What is the hard deadline and who is impacted?' before switching tasks.
Complain to the team that they wasted your time.
Only do what is on your calendar and refuse any changes.

dynamicUpdate.explanation: Clarifying deadline and impact prevents derailment from your active commitments.

questions.title: The Mid-Session Distraction
questions.scenario:
You are 15 minutes into teaching a live coding class with 18 students. Your mentor sends you a private Slack message:

'Hey, please send me the student roster for Grade 6 right now.'

What is your best response?

options.text: Stop the class, open Excel, find the roster, and send it immediately.
Ignore the message completely until the end of the day.
Give students a 2-minute independent challenge, reply quickly: 'Currently teaching live until 12:00. Will send immediately at 12:05 PM', and continue teaching.
Reply with 'Busy!' and mute your laptop.

questions.explanation: Classroom delivery is sacred. Never compromise student experience for back-office requests. A quick acknowledgment with an exact ETA manages expectations professionally.
questions.learningObjective: Acknowledge promptly with an ETA without abandoning your live classroom.
questions.discussionQuestion: What happens to instructor credibility when you look away from the students to do admin work?

It is 10:15 AM. You are preparing your slides for an 11:30 AM school session. Four notifications pop up simultaneously:

🔴 A mentor pings: 'Need urgent confirmation if you can take an extra class at 2:00 PM today.'
🟠 A teammate asks: 'Can you review my Scratch project before my class in 3 hours?'
🟡 Admin reminder: 'Submit your weekly attendance log before 5:00 PM today.'
🔥 WhatsApp group message: 'URGENT!! Need someone to update the slide deck ASAP!!'

Which task do you address FIRST?

options.text: Drop everything and fix the 'URGENT!!' slide deck.
Help your teammate review their Scratch project immediately.
Complete your 11:30 AM preparation first, then reply to the mentor about the 2:00 PM class.
Rush to fill in the weekly attendance log to get admin off your back.

questions.explanation: Your immediate commitment is the 11:30 AM class happening in 75 minutes. The mentor's 2:00 PM request has a clear time window, whereas 'URGENT' without context or deadline is often fake urgency.
questions.learningObjective: Prioritize by real deadline & direct classroom impact, not by who types in ALL CAPS.
questions.discussionQuestion: Why do we instinctively jump to whoever writes 'URGENT' in capital letters?
questions.facilitatorTips: Ask the room: 'Who chose A? Why does the word URGENT trigger panic?'

dynamicUpdate.announcement: 🚨 PLOT REVEAL: The person who sent 'URGENT!! slide deck' actually needs it for next Thursday's marketing meeting!
dynamicUpdate.questionText: Now that you know this, what is the professional rule for incoming 'urgent' tasks?

options.text: Ignore all WhatsApp messages forever.
Always ask: 'What is the hard deadline and who is impacted?' before switching tasks.
Complain to the team that they wasted your time.
Only do what is on your calendar and refuse any changes.

dynamicUpdate.explanation: Clarifying deadline and impact prevents derailment from your active commitments.

questions.title: The Mid-Session Distraction
questions.scenario:
You are 15 minutes into teaching a live coding class with 18 students. Your mentor sends you a private Slack message:

'Hey, please send me the student roster for Grade 6 right now.'

What is your best response?

options.text: Stop the class, open Excel, find the roster, and send it immediately.
Ignore the message completely until the end of the day.
Give students a 2-minute independent challenge, reply quickly: 'Currently teaching live until 12:00. Will send immediately at 12:05 PM', and continue teaching.
Reply with 'Busy!' and mute your laptop.

questions.explanation: Classroom delivery is sacred. Never compromise student experience for back-office requests. A quick acknowledgment with an exact ETA manages expectations professionally.
questions.learningObjective: Acknowledge promptly with an ETA without abandoning your live classroom.
questions.discussionQuestion: What happens to instructor credibility when you look away from the students to do admin work?

game.title: Game 2: The Plot Twist
game.subtitle: Adaptability under pressure - breaking news rounds
game.description: Simulates sudden real-world classroom twists. Players must pause, clarify, and adapt gracefully.

questions.title: Breaking News: Round 1
questions.scenario:
🚨 BREAKING UPDATE #1: You spent 2 hours thoroughly preparing an advanced Python session for Grade 5 scheduled at 4:00 PM.

At 3:40 PM (20 minutes before class), the B2B coordinator pings you:
'SURPRISE: The school requested switching to Grade 3 block-based Scratch instead of Python!'

What is your very first reaction?

options.text: Panic and tell the coordinator: 'I can't do this, find someone else.'
Pause 30 seconds. Check if you have Grade 3 Scratch materials ready in your drive, clarify student prior experience, and confirm.
Teach Python anyway because that's what you prepared.
Argue with the school coordinator about short notice.

questions.explanation: Adaptability is our core B2B value. Pausing prevents emotional escalation, checking assets gives clarity, and confirming gives the client confidence.
questions.learningObjective: Framework: Pause → Clarify → Check Assets → Confirm.
questions.discussionQuestion: How do you keep your cool when the entire lesson plan flips 20 minutes before kickoff?

questions.title: Breaking News: Round 2 (The Tech Glitch)
questions.scenario:
🚨 BREAKING UPDATE #2: You log into the classroom with the Grade 3 students. Half the students cannot open Scratch because the school firewall blocks the online editor!

You have 40 minutes left in the session. What do you do?

options.text: Cancel the class and log off.
Spend 35 minutes trying to debug the school network settings on each computer.
Switch seamlessly to offline Scratch Desktop if installed, or do an engaging interactive algorithmic thinking / unplugged game while the mentor alerts school IT.
Tell the kids: 'Sorry, your school has bad internet' and sit silently.

questions.explanation: Always have an 'unplugged' or offline fallback. Great instructors can teach computational thinking with a whiteboard, a story, or paper if technology fails.
questions.learningObjective: Never let technical failure stop learning: have an offline / unplugged contingency.
questions.discussionQuestion: What is your personal 'Plan B' when the internet completely dies during a live session?

game.title: Game 1: Urgent or Fake Urgent?
game.subtitle: Distinguish actual urgency from things that just sound loud
game.description: Teach participants to assess true business impact and deadlines rather than panicking over loud requests.

questions.title: The Quadruple Ping
questions.scenario:
It is 10:15 AM. You are preparing your slides for an 11:30 AM school session. Four notifications pop up simultaneously:

🔴 A mentor pings: 'Need urgent confirmation if you can take an extra class at 2:00 PM today.'
🟠 A teammate asks: 'Can you review my Scratch project before my class in 3 hours?'
🟡 Admin reminder: 'Submit your weekly attendance log before 5:00 PM today.'
🔥 WhatsApp group message: 'URGENT!! Need someone to update the slide deck ASAP!!'

Which task do you address FIRST?

options.text: Drop everything and fix the 'URGENT!!' slide deck.
Help your teammate review their Scratch project immediately.
Complete your 11:30 AM preparation first, then reply to the mentor about the 2:00 PM class.
Rush to fill in the weekly attendance log to get admin off your back.

questions.explanation: Your immediate commitment is the 11:30 AM class happening in 75 minutes. The mentor's 2:00 PM request has a clear time window, whereas 'URGENT' without context or deadline is often fake urgency.
questions.learningObjective: Prioritize by real deadline & direct classroom impact, not by who types in ALL CAPS.
questions.discussionQuestion: Why do we instinctively jump to whoever writes 'URGENT' in capital letters?
questions.facilitatorTips: Ask the room: 'Who chose A? Why does the word URGENT trigger panic?'

dynamicUpdate.announcement: 🚨 PLOT REVEAL: The person who sent 'URGENT!! slide deck' actually needs it for next Thursday's marketing meeting!
dynamicUpdate.questionText: Now that you know this, what is the professional rule for incoming 'urgent' tasks?

options.text: Ignore all WhatsApp messages forever.
Always ask: 'What is the hard deadline and who is impacted?' before switching tasks.
Complain to the team that they wasted your time.
Only do what is on your calendar and refuse any changes.

dynamicUpdate.explanation: Clarifying deadline and impact prevents derailment from your active commitments.

questions.title: The Mid-Session Distraction
questions.scenario:
You are 15 minutes into teaching a live coding class with 18 students. Your mentor sends you a private Slack message:

'Hey, please send me the student roster for Grade 6 right now.'

What is your best response?

options.text: Stop the class, open Excel, find the roster, and send it immediately.
Ignore the message completely until the end of the day.
Give students a 2-minute independent challenge, reply quickly: 'Currently teaching live until 12:00. Will send immediately at 12:05 PM', and continue teaching.
Reply with 'Busy!' and mute your laptop.

questions.explanation: Classroom delivery is sacred. Never compromise student experience for back-office requests. A quick acknowledgment with an exact ETA manages expectations professionally.
questions.learningObjective: Acknowledge promptly with an ETA without abandoning your live classroom.
questions.discussionQuestion: What happens to instructor credibility when you look away from the students to do admin work?

game.title: Game 4: WhatsApp Court
game.subtitle: Egyptian workplace communication - Judge the message!
game.description: Real Egyptian workplace WhatsApp messages. Rate them as Professional vs Unprofessional and analyze realistic alternatives.

questions.title: WhatsApp Case #1: The Blunt Rejection
questions.scenario:
📱 Saturday 8:00 PM. Mentor pings instructor:
'Hey Omar! Could you cover tomorrow's 9:00 AM session at School X?'

Instructor replies at 11:30 PM:
'مش هقدر.' (Can't.)

Is this message PROFESSIONAL or UNPROFESSIONAL?

options.text: 👍 Professional (Short, clear, direct)
👎 Unprofessional (Blunt, lacks context, late, no alternative)

questions.explanation: While setting boundaries is healthy, sending a 2-word rejection late at night gives zero context or alternative, leaving the team stranded.
questions.learningObjective: Saying NO professionally: 'I won't be able to cover tomorrow at 9 AM due to prior commitment, but I can take any slot after 1 PM or help prep materials.'
questions.discussionQuestion: How can you protect your personal time while remaining a supportive teammate?

questions.title: WhatsApp Case #2: The Ghosting Over-Explainer
questions.scenario:
📱 Mentor sends a message at 2:00 PM asking for session feedback.
Instructor reads it immediately (blue double checks), disappears for 24 hours, then sends a 4-minute voice note explaining their personal internet issues, grocery run, and family lunch.

Is this PROFESSIONAL or UNPROFESSIONAL?

options.text: 👍 Professional (They explained everything in detail)
👎 Unprofessional (Over-explaining personal life + delayed communication)

questions.explanation: Professional communication requires timely acknowledgment, not long emotional voice notes about personal errands. A quick 1-sentence typed reply is 100x better.
questions.learningObjective: Be concise and timely. Don't ghost then over-explain your personal life.
questions.discussionQuestion: Why do young professionals feel the need to give huge medical/personal justifications instead of simple professional timelines?

questions.title: WhatsApp Case #3: The Proactive Boundary
questions.scenario:
📱 Mentor: 'Can you take an extra 3 sessions this week in Alexandria?'

Instructor: 'Thanks for thinking of me! I can commit to 1 session on Wednesday, but my university exam schedule prevents me from taking the other two. Let me know if Wednesday works so I can lock it in.'

Is this message PROFESSIONAL?

options.text: 👍 Professional (Clear, appreciative, realistic boundaries)
👎 Unprofessional (Should say yes to all sessions)

questions.explanation: This is gold-standard B2B behavior! Warm, appreciates the offer, sets realistic constraints, and commits reliably to what they can deliver.
questions.learningObjective: Realistic commitment is better than over-promising and failing.
questions.discussionQuestion: Why is an instructor who says 'I can reliably do 1 class' more valuable than one who says 'I will do all 3' and fails to show up?

game.title: Game 4: WhatsApp Court
game.subtitle: Egyptian workplace communication - Judge the message!
game.description: Real Egyptian workplace WhatsApp messages. Rate them as Professional vs Unprofessional and analyze realistic alternatives.

questions.title: WhatsApp Case #1: The Blunt Rejection
questions.scenario:
📱 Saturday 8:00 PM. Mentor pings instructor:
'Hey Omar! Could you cover tomorrow's 9:00 AM session at School X?'

Instructor replies at 11:30 PM:
'مش هقدر.' (Can't.)

Is this message PROFESSIONAL or UNPROFESSIONAL?

options.text: 👍 Professional (Short, clear, direct)
👎 Unprofessional (Blunt, lacks context, late, no alternative)

questions.explanation: While setting boundaries is healthy, sending a 2-word rejection late at night gives zero context or alternative, leaving the team stranded.
questions.learningObjective: Saying NO professionally: 'I won't be able to cover tomorrow at 9 AM due to prior commitment, but I can take any slot after 1 PM or help prep materials.'
questions.discussionQuestion: How can you protect your personal time while remaining a supportive teammate?

questions.title: WhatsApp Case #2: The Ghosting Over-Explainer
questions.scenario:
📱 Mentor sends a message at 2:00 PM asking for session feedback.
Instructor reads it immediately (blue double checks), disappears for 24 hours, then sends a 4-minute voice note explaining their personal internet issues, grocery run, and family lunch.

Is this PROFESSIONAL or UNPROFESSIONAL?

options.text: 👍 Professional (They explained everything in detail)
👎 Unprofessional (Over-explaining personal life + delayed communication)

questions.explanation: Professional communication requires timely acknowledgment, not long emotional voice notes about personal errands. A quick 1-sentence typed reply is 100x better.
questions.learningObjective: Be concise and timely. Don't ghost then over-explain your personal life.
questions.discussionQuestion: Why do young professionals feel the need to give huge medical/personal justifications instead of simple professional timelines?

questions.title: WhatsApp Case #3: The Proactive Boundary
questions.scenario:
📱 Mentor: 'Can you take an extra 3 sessions this week in Alexandria?'

Instructor: 'Thanks for thinking of me! I can commit to 1 session on Wednesday, but my university exam schedule prevents me from taking the other two. Let me know if Wednesday works so I can lock it in.'

Is this message PROFESSIONAL?

options.text: 👍 Professional (Clear, appreciative, realistic boundaries)
👎 Unprofessional (Should say yes to all sessions)

questions.explanation: This is gold-standard B2B behavior! Warm, appreciates the offer, sets realistic constraints, and commits reliably to what they can deliver.
questions.learningObjective: Realistic commitment is better than over-promising and failing.
questions.discussionQuestion: Why is an instructor who says 'I can reliably do 1 class' more valuable than one who says 'I will do all 3' and fails to show up?

game.subtitle: The Ultimate 45-Minute Emergency Simulation
game.description: Collaborative team challenge simulating a real live workshop emergency with progressive clues.

questions.title: 🚨 The 45-Minute Emergency: Clue Sequence
questions.scenario:
Time is 8:15 AM. A flagship B2B partner school session begins at 9:00 AM sharp (45 mins away).

• CLUE 1: The assigned instructor just called in sick with acute food poisoning.
• CLUE 2: The class has 24 Grade 6 students expecting Robotics.
• CLUE 3: The school lab has internet, but robotics kits are locked in a cabinet.
• CLUE 4: You have another meeting scheduled at 10:00 AM.
• CLUE 5: Teammate Nour is free until 11:00 AM and lives 10 mins away.

What is your team's optimal coordinated action plan?

options.text: Cancel the school session and apologize to the principal.
You take the 9:00 AM kick-off online/onsite with an unplugged/simulator activity, coordinate with Nour to take over at 9:45 AM, and alert the B2B Ops Lead to authorize key handover.
Leave your 10:00 AM meeting unattended without telling anyone.
Tell the sick instructor to show up anyway.

questions.explanation: Outstanding leadership! You protect the student experience, mobilize available team capacity (Nour), communicate with Ops, and honor your 10:00 AM commitment.
questions.learningObjective: Triage → Mobilize Team → Protect Client Experience → Honor Commitments.
questions.discussionQuestion: How do great teams act like a relay race rather than isolated islands?

dynamicUpdate.announcement: 🚨 PLOT REVEAL: The person who sent 'URGENT!! slide deck' actually needs it for next Thursday's marketing meeting!
dynamicUpdate.questionText: Now that you know this, what is the professional rule for incoming 'urgent' tasks?

options.text: Ignore all WhatsApp messages forever.
Always ask: 'What is the hard deadline and who is impacted?' before switching tasks.
Complain to the team that they wasted your time.
Only do what is on your calendar and refuse any changes.

dynamicUpdate.explanation: Clarifying deadline and impact prevents derailment from your active commitments.

questions.title: The Mid-Session Distraction
questions.scenario:
You are 15 minutes into teaching a live coding class with 18 students. Your mentor sends you a private Slack message:

'Hey, please send me the student roster for Grade 6 right now.'

What is your best response?

options.text: Stop the class, open Excel, find the roster, and send it immediately.
Ignore the message completely until the end of the day.
Give students a 2-minute independent challenge, reply quickly: 'Currently teaching live until 12:00. Will send immediately at 12:05 PM', and continue teaching.
Reply with 'Busy!' and mute your laptop.

questions.explanation: Classroom delivery is sacred. Never compromise student experience for back-office requests. A quick acknowledgment with an exact ETA manages expectations professionally.
questions.learningObjective: Acknowledge promptly with an ETA without abandoning your live classroom.
questions.discussionQuestion: What happens to instructor credibility when you look away from the students to do admin work?

game.title: Game 1: Urgent or Fake Urgent?
game.subtitle: Distinguish actual urgency from things that just sound loud
game.description: Teach participants to assess true business impact and deadlines rather than panicking over loud requests.

questions.title: The Quadruple Ping
questions.scenario:
It is 10:15 AM. You are preparing your slides for an 11:30 AM school session. Four notifications pop up simultaneously:

🔴 A mentor pings: 'Need urgent confirmation if you can take an extra class at 2:00 PM today.'
🟠 A teammate asks: 'Can you review my Scratch project before my class in 3 hours?'
🟡 Admin reminder: 'Submit your weekly attendance log before 5:00 PM today.'
🔥 WhatsApp group message: 'URGENT!! Need someone to update the slide deck ASAP!!'

Which task do you address FIRST?

options.text: Drop everything and fix the 'URGENT!!' slide deck.
Help your teammate review their Scratch project immediately.
Complete your 11:30 AM preparation first, then reply to the mentor about the 2:00 PM class.
Rush to fill in the weekly attendance log to get admin off your back.

questions.explanation: Your immediate commitment is the 11:30 AM class happening in 75 minutes. The mentor's 2:00 PM request has a clear time window, whereas 'URGENT' without context or deadline is often fake urgency.
questions.learningObjective: Prioritize by real deadline & direct classroom impact, not by who types in ALL CAPS.
